questions.question: He gave the book to ___.
questions.explanation: After a preposition the objective form is required.
questions.bn: Preposition-এর পরে objective case হয়। তাই ‘me’।

questions.question: It was ___ who helped me.
questions.explanation: When the pronoun is subject of a following clause, use nominative.
questions.bn: পরবর্তী clause-এর subject হলে nominative হয়।

questions.question: Between you and ___ there is no secret.
questions.explanation: ‘Between’ is a preposition and takes the objective case.

questions.question: He is taller than ___.
questions.explanation: Formal: than I (am). Colloquial ‘me’ is common but formal prefers nominative.

questions.question: Let ___ go to the market.
questions.explanation: ‘Let’ is followed by the objective case.

questions.question: This book is ___, not yours.
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun stands alone without a noun.

questions.question: Nobody was present there but ___.
questions.explanation: ‘But’ used as preposition takes objective case.

questions.question: The boy is known to him and ___.
questions.explanation: Both pronouns must be in the same (objective) case.

questions.question: Which is correct formal English?
questions.explanation: After verb ‘to be’ formal English uses nominative.

questions.question: One must do ___ duty.
I know the man ___ came yesterday.
questions.explanation: ‘Who’ is nominative and refers to persons.

questions.question: He is a person ___ you can trust.
This is the book ___ I bought.
He is the best man ___ I have ever seen.
There is no man ___ wishes to be happy.
This is the same book ___ I lost.
Only such boys ___ have passed need apply.
I who ___ your teacher advise you.
questions.explanation: Relative agrees with antecedent in person: I → am.

questions.question: To ___ did you give the letter?
questions.explanation: After a preposition formal English uses whom.

questions.question: The boys ___ were present are my friends.
Work and play are both necessary; ___ gives us rest.
These oranges are not ripe; please send me some ripe ___.
questions.explanation: Ones stands for the plural noun previously mentioned.

questions.question: I said ___.
If you are my friend, show yourself as ___.
questions.explanation: ‘Such’ stands for the noun/phrase already mentioned.

questions.question: ___ is he? — He is a doctor.
___ of these pens is yours?
questions.explanation: Which selects one from a group.

questions.question: ___ are you speaking to?
Neither of them ___ present.
Each of the girls has done ___ work.
Either of the two roads ___ lead to the station.
I hurt ___.
questions.explanation: Reflexive: subject and object are the same person.
questions.bn: কর্তা ও কর্ম একই ব্যক্তি হলে reflexive।

questions.question: I ___ saw the accident.
Which is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Emphatic pronoun cannot stand alone as subject.
questions.bn: Emphatic একা subject হতে পারে না।

questions.question: ___ say that the train is late.
None of them ___ arrived yet.
questions.explanation: None can take singular (or plural). Both acceptable; singular is safer in formal.
questions.bn: None singular বা plural হতে পারে।

questions.question: The two brothers help ___.
questions.explanation: Traditionally each other is used for two.

questions.question: The students in the class helped ___.
questions.explanation: One another is preferred for more than two.

questions.question: Whose bag is this? It is ___.
The correct form is:
questions.explanation: Possessive of it is ‘its’ (no apostrophe). It’s = it is.

questions.question: He knows you better than ___.
questions.explanation: Than I = than I know you; than me = than he knows me.
questions.bn: অর্থ অনুযায়ী I বা me দুটোই সম্ভব।

questions.question: Fill in: She is as clever as ___ (I / me).
questions.explanation: As I (am) — nominative in formal English.

questions.question: Fill in: It was ___ who broke the window. (he / him)
Fill in: The girl ___ you met is my sister. (who / whom)
Fill in: All ___ glitters is not gold. (that / which)
We (the editor) support the bill. This ‘we’ is called:
questions.explanation: Newspaper editors use ‘we’ for the paper.

questions.question: The baby is crying for ___ mother.
questions.explanation: For babies sex is often not specified → it/its.

questions.question: He passed the exam, ___ pleased his parents.
questions.explanation: Which can refer to a whole preceding clause.
questions.bn: Which পুরো clause-কে নির্দেশ করতে পারে।

questions.question: Identify the pronoun type: ‘Whoever comes is welcome.’
Correct: The book may be given to Ram or ___.
He availed ___ of the opportunity.
Many are called but ___ are chosen.
questions.explanation: ‘Few’ is used as an indefinite pronoun here.

questions.question: You and ___ must finish the work.
The man ___ house was burnt is crying.
His house is bigger than ___ of Jadu.
___ do you prefer — tea or coffee?
questions.bn: সীমিত বিকল্প থেকে বেছে নিতে which।

questions.question: It is five o’clock now. Here ‘it’ refers to:
It was with difficulty that I did it. ‘It’ is used for:
Wrong sentence:
options: The man who came is my uncle
The man whom I saw is my uncle
The man whom came is my uncle
The man who I saw is my uncle (informal)
questions.answer: The man whom came is my uncle

questions.question: Each of them ___ a prize.
Classify: ‘This is the dog which I saw.’
